reasoning_trace: validate_providers admits allow_insecure_endpoint for every non-CLI provider type. TransportPolicy is constructed only in openai_adapter.py (_transport_policy line 217, health_check line 858); anthropic_adapter.py:334 and google_adapter.py call http_post_stream/http_post with no policy. Executed: a type: anthropic provider with endpoint http://10.0.0.5:8080 and allow_insecure_endpoint 10.0.0.5 loads cleanly through the head loader. Dissent DISS-C-002 confirmed.
finding: Insecure-endpoint opt-in is admitted for provider types whose adapter applies none of the promised request-time rules
critique: The example config promises no proxy, no redirects and a path-prefix rule 'for this provider'; that holds for OpenAI-type providers only.
remediation: Refuse allow_insecure_endpoint at load unless the provider type is openai/openai_compat, or construct the TransportPolicy in ProviderAdapter so every adapter's http_* call receives it.

reasoning_trace: Nothing ties dispatch_group: local to a loopback/RFC1918/opt-in endpoint. Executed: hop-locality.py classifies lanbox:m1 (endpoint https://llm.example.com/v1, model dispatch_group: local) as local, and the head loader loads it. Under local_voices such a hop is planned, dispatched (TransportPolicy restricts proxies/redirects/path, not the destination) and recorded hop_locality: local.
finding: The local_voices posture trusts the dispatch_group label; a hosted https endpoint labelled local is planned, dispatched and audited as local
critique: The one control meant to keep prompts on the host is a self-declared label with no consistency check against the endpoint it governs.
remediation: At load, warn or refuse when a dispatch_group: local model's provider endpoint is not loopback, RFC1918 or the provider's opt-in host; record the endpoint class beside hop_locality in MODELINV.

code_snippet: return "response_format" in text or "json_schema" in text
reasoning_trace: Any HTTP 400 whose body mentions response_format or json_schema triggers one retry without the schema (lines 191-204). OpenAI strict-mode schema errors ('Invalid schema for response_format ...') match too, and a server controls both status and body. _build_chat_body always sends strict: true (line 441). The downgrade is recorded (schema_rejected_by_server) but not surfaced beyond a WARN. Review MEDIUM and dissent DISS-C-004 agree.
finding: 400 heuristic lets a supported-but-strict-rejecting server, or any hostile server, silently downgrade structured output and receive the prompt twice
critique: The heuristic cannot distinguish 'unsupported feature' from 'your schema is wrong'; the operator who declared structured_json loses enforcement without a visible failure.
remediation: Narrow to the error object's param/code fields; treat 'invalid schema'/'additionalProperties' phrasings as a schema defect (raise or retry once with strict: false); add the OpenAI strict-mode message as a negative case in test_the_heuristic.

code_snippet: exit keys follow the trusted-source precedence below even when the checkout is a PR head.
reasoning_trace: loadTrustedConfig refuses only head-only keyless/insecure declarations (config.ts:684-686). Every voice dispatches through cheval, whose loader reads the working tree's .loa.config.yaml (the PR head on a PR-head checkout); validate_declared_endpoint admits any https DNS host. On such a checkout the head still controls the endpoint of a built-in provider and cheval would send that provider's credential to it. Pre-existing exposure (#1050 says no PR-head checkout is shipped), but the PR's new sentence claims protection in exactly that scenario.
finding: Documented trusted-config protection is broader than the control: only two flags are refused, cheval's own config read is unprotected on a PR-head checkout
critique: False assurance in the trust contract is itself a defect: an operator reading SKILL.md:118 could adopt a PR-head checkout believing provider declarations are trusted-source only.
remediation: Either scope the sentence to what is refused (keyless and allow_insecure_endpoint), or pass the trusted provider view to cheval (e.g. a LOA_HOUNFOUR_TRUSTED_CONFIG path) so endpoints and aliases also come from the trusted source.

reasoning_trace: Executed: the head loader resolves a templated endpoint (https://{env:AUDIT_HOST}/v1) to a plain str before validate_providers. describe_provider emits that resolved string verbatim; model-health-probe.sh:1505 logs it.
